chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn Hisham al-Mu'addab (RA) narrated: Muhammad ibn Abu Abdillah al-Kufi narrated: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Khazzaz al-Kufi narrated: Sulayman ibn Ja'far narrated: Ali ibn al-Hakam narrated: Hisham ibn Salim said: I was in the presence of Muhammad ibn al-Nu'man al-Ahwal, when a man stood up before him and asked him, 'How did you recognize your Lord?' He replied, 'By His Direction, His Instruction, His Introduction, and His Guidance.' I left his presence and met Hisham ibn al-Hakam, so I asked him, 'What should I say to someone who asks me: how did you recognize your Lord?'

He said: If someone asked me: 'With what did you recognize your Lord?' I would say: I recognized Allah, High be His Glory, through my own self, because it is the thing closest to me. I find it composed of assembled parts and formed of components, with clear structure and evident craftsmanship, manifesting various patterns of design and form, increasing after decrease, and decreasing after increase. He has created for it diverse senses and distinct limbs - sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch - innate in weakness, deficiency, and humility. None of them perceives the function of the other, nor do they have strength over one another. They are incapable of attracting benefits to themselves or repelling harm from themselves. It became impossible in the intellect that there be a compilation without a compiler, and a fixed form without a form-maker. Thus, I knew that it has a Creator who created it, and a Form-maker who formed it, Who is contrary to it in all aspects.
Allah, the Mighty and High, has said: 'And in your own souls (too); will you not then see?'
ai.seo_question: How does recognizing oneself lead to recognizing God according to Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* articulates the Shia theological concept of *al-‘ilm bi-nafs al-insan* (knowing God through the self), arguing that the intricate composition and inherent fragility of the human body serve as empirical proof of a distinct Creator. The narrative highlights the transition from observing the 'parts' to recognizing the 'Maker,' emphasizing that God’s essence is fundamentally different from His creation (*mukhalifa laha*). This rational approach to monotheism underscores the Shia emphasis on using intellect (*‘aql*) alongside revelation to establish divine unity.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 9. Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn Hisham al-Mu`addab (RA) said: Muhammad ibn Abu `Abd Allah al-Kufi said: Muhammad ibn Isma`il al-Barmaki said: Muhammad ibn `Abd alRahman al-Khazzaz al-Kufi said: Sulayman ibn Ja`far said: `Ali ibn al-Hakam said: Hisham ibn Salim said I was in the presence of Muhammad ibn al-Mu`man al-Ahwal, when a man stood up before him, and asked him, “How did you recognize your Lord?” He replied, “By means of His Direction, His Instruction, His Introduction, and His Guidance.” He says: I left his presence, and met with Hisham ibn al-Hakam, so I asked him, “What should I say to someone who asks me: how did you recognize your Lord?”

Hisham relied, “If someone asked me: what did you recognize your Lord with? I would say: I recognized Allah, High be His Glory, though my own body as that is the thing which is the closest to me. Verily, my body is composed of assembled parts and formed of components which were created, the subject of intelligent design, and engineering. My body increases after decrease, and is reduced after enlargement. My body has different senses, like sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch, as well as different limbs. My body was created in weakness, deficiency and contempt. None of the sense can perceive the function of the other, nor do they have strength over others. They are incapable of attracting benefits to themselves and preventing harm to themselves. Wisdom dictates that it is impossible for something to be compiled without a compiler, and that it is impossible for an image to be made without an artist. Thus, I learned that my body has a Creator, and that my image was made by an Artist, Who is contrary to them from all dimensions.
Allah, the Mighty and High, has said: And in your own souls (too); will you not then see.
